# Node types

Every node type: what it does, its ports (`name: data type`) and its parameters (type, default, unit, limits). A parameter whose type is a link is a table; its fields are under *Value types*. Graphs: [graphs.md](graphs.md); how to change things: [README.md](README.md).

## classes.bands

Version 1

Classes by value bands, e.g. biomes by effective height.

Inputs: `field: field`  
Outputs: `classes: classes`

Parameters:

- `limits` (list of number, required): Borders between the classes (ascending).
- `first` (integer, default `1`, >= 0, <= 255): Code of the lowest class; the next band gets first + 1 and so on.

## classes.majority

Version 1

Each pixel takes the class most frequent around it: smooth, natural borders without specks.

Inputs: `classes: classes`  
Outputs: `classes: classes`

Parameters:

- `codes` (list of integer, required): The classes that compete; every pixel gets one of them.
- `radius_m` (number, default `80.0`, unit m, > 0): Gaussian radius (real metres) of the vote.

## classes.select

Version 1

Pixels whose class is one of `codes`.

Inputs: `classes: classes`  
Outputs: `mask: mask`

Parameters:

- `codes` (list of integer, required): Class codes that form the mask.

## classes.to_map

Version 1

The class map on the heightmap grid (nearest neighbour).

Inputs: `classes: classes`  
Outputs: `classes: classes`

## climate.reference

Version 1

Reference height of the climate mod: the map's lowest land rounded to the nearest step (550 and 560 -> 600).
The heightmap keeps the exact lowest land; the mod's height rules shift by the difference (at most half a step
of real elevation; rounded up, they appear lower on the map).

Inputs: `land_min_m: number`  
Outputs: `reference_m: number`

Parameters:

- `step_m` (number, default `100.0`, unit m, >= 0): Round the map's lowest land to this step (0 = exact), so maps with a similar lowest land share one mod.

## elevation.read

Version 1

Reads the elevation model (a GeoTIFF), optionally only a crop given in WGS84 degrees.

Inputs: -  
Outputs: `source: elevation_source`

Parameters:

- `path` (string, default `""`): GeoTIFF of the elevation model (empty: downloaded, see `download`).
- `crop` ([GeoBounds](#geobounds) \| none, default `null`): Part of the file to read (None = all).
- `download` ([DemDownload](#demdownload) \| none, default `null`): Without a path: download the crop from OpenTopography (once, into the download folder).

## elevation.read_on_map

Version 1

The original elevation model on the heightmap grid, resampled bilinearly while reading (no levelling, gaps
filled with the nearest height) - what the river planning measures valleys on.

Inputs: `map_format: map_format`  
Outputs: `heights: field`

Parameters:

- `path` (string, default `""`): GeoTIFF of the elevation model (empty: downloaded, see `download`).
- `crop` ([GeoBounds](#geobounds) \| none, default `null`): Part of the file to read (None = all).
- `download` ([DemDownload](#demdownload) \| none, default `null`): Without a path: download the crop from OpenTopography (once, into the download folder).
- `rotation_deg` (0 \| 90 \| 180 \| 270, default `0`): Direction of the map's top edge, clockwise from north.

## elevation.references

Version 1

Height references: lowest land (water line) and black of the heightmap (bottom of real water).

Inputs: `heights: field`  
Outputs: `land_min_m: number`, `black_m: number`

Parameters:

- `min_height_m` (number \| none, default `null`, unit m): Lowest land = game height 0 (water line); None = the lowest point of the map.
- `water_sink_m` (number, default `40.0`, unit m, >= 0): Real water core this much below the lowest land (black of the heightmap).

Version 1

Fills gaps (nearest valid height), turns the raster to the map orientation and resamples it bicubically to the

Parameters:

## farmland.close_gap

Version 1

Narrow strips of another layer (meadow, forest) between fields become cropland - except `keep` (e.g.

## farmland.field_paths

Version 1

Signed distance to the parcel borders (grey 127.5 = border), for paths between the fields: parcels two-coloured
along a maximum spanning tree of the border lengths, so conflicts remain only at short contacts.

Inputs: `parcels: labels`  
Outputs: `image: image`

Parameters:

- `range_game_m` (number, default `32.0`, unit game m, > 0): Distance for grey 0 / 255.

## farmland.osm_fields

Version 1

OSM fields rasterised (not on water/border), small neighbours merged into groups, one crop per group (from the
OSM crop tag, else drawn by size class so that neighbours differ). `fields` = all field pixels, `crop_type` = crop
per pixel (0 = grass).

Inputs: `areas: osm_areas`, `no_cover: mask`  
Outputs: `fields: mask`, `groups: labels`, `crop_type: classes`, `group_count: integer`

Parameters:

- `seed` (integer, default `3`): Random seed of the crop choice.
- `merge_gap_game_m` (number, default `8.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Fields with at most this gap count as neighbours.
- `min_game_ha` (number, default `1.0`, unit game ha, >= 0): Smaller groups are merged with neighbours.
- `max_game_ha` (number, default `4.0`, unit game ha, >= 0): Merging only up to this group size.
- `crops` ([CropPlan](#cropplan), default `{"shares": {"corn": 0.2, "soil": 0.1, "wheat": 0.4}, "by_size": [{"min_game_ha": 1.5, "shares": {"co ...`): Crop types (from the climate preset).

## farmland.osm_preview

Version 1

Half resolution: colour per crop, brightness per group, group borders dark; cropland without OSM field in
khaki.

Inputs: `crop_type: classes`, `groups: labels`, `group_count: integer`, `cropland: mask`  
Outputs: `preview: image`

Parameters:

- `seed` (integer, default `3`): The seed of the field node (brightness per group).

## farmland.parcels

Version 1

Each field area in a grid of rectangles (along the contour lines on slopes, else along its main axis), large
areas in field blocks first; one crop per parcel by the crop plan's shares.

Inputs: `cropland: mask`, `heights: field`  
Outputs: `parcels: labels`, `crop_type: classes`, `farm_grid: farm_grid`, `preview: image`

Parameters:

- `seed` (integer, default `3`): Random seed of the parcels and the crop choice.
- `min_split_game_ha` (number, default `1.0`, unit game ha, >= 0): Smaller fields are not divided.
- `block_game_m` (number, default `2500.0`, unit game m, > 0): Large areas in field blocks of about this size.
- `block_turn_deg` (number, default `10.0`, unit deg, >= 0): Block direction differs from the area by at most this.
- `width_game_m` ([number, number], default `[50.0, 150.0]`): Strip width across the working direction (game m).
- `length_game_m` ([number, number], default `[100.0, 300.0]`): Parcel length along it (game m).
- `min_aspect` (number, default `1.5`): Length at least this times the width.
- `jitter` (number, default `0.15`): Line spacing varied by up to this share.
- `min_side_game_m` (number, default `50.0`, unit game m, > 0): Smallest side (reference of the minimum area).
- `min_area_share` (number, default `0.5`): Edge pieces smaller than share x min side² join a neighbour.
- `size_bias` (number, default `0.5`): Exponent of the random size (< 1 = larger parcels more often).
- `contour_slope_deg` (number, default `4.0`, unit deg, >= 0): From this mean slope: parcels along the contour lines.
- `crops` ([CropPlan](#cropplan), default `{"shares": {"corn": 0.2, "soil": 0.1, "wheat": 0.4}, "by_size": [{"min_game_ha": 1.5, "shares": {"co ...`): Crop types (from the climate preset).

## field.at_least

Version 1

Raises every value below `minimum` to it (e.g. land below the water line).

Inputs: `field: field`, `minimum: number`  
Outputs: `field: field`

## field.min_within

Version 1

Lowest value within a circle around each pixel, e.g. the valley floor next to a river.

Inputs: `field: field`  
Outputs: `field: field`

Parameters:

- `radius_px` (integer, default `1`, >= 1): Radius in pixels of the field (heightmap grid: 1 px = 4 game m).

## field.noise

Version 1

Smooth random noise on the grid of `like`.

Inputs: `like: field`  
Outputs: `noise: field`

Parameters:

- `seed` (integer, default `1`): Random seed; the same seed gives the same noise.
- `wave_m` (number, default `300.0`, unit m, > 0): Typical size of the bumps (real metres).
- `amplitude` (number, default `80.0`, >= 0): Standard deviation of the result.

## field.ramp

Version 1

max(0, value - start) x per_unit, e.g. extra height for steep slopes.

Inputs: `field: field`  
Outputs: `field: field`

Parameters:

- `start` (number, default `0.0`): Below this value the result is 0.
- `per_unit` (number, default `1.0`): Increase of the result per unit above `start`.

## field.resample

Version 1

The field on a grid of 1/work_scale of the heightmap resolution.

Inputs: `field: field`  
Outputs: `field: field`

Parameters:

- `work_scale` (integer, default `4`, >= 1): Result has 1/work_scale of the heightmap resolution (1 = heightmap grid).
- `method` ("box" \| "bilinear" \| "bicubic" \| "nearest", default `"box"`): Box averages (coarser grids); bicubic/bilinear interpolate (finer grids).

## field.slope

Version 1

Slope of a height field in degrees.

Inputs: `field: field`  
Outputs: `degrees: field`

## field.smooth

Gaussian smoothing.

## industries.plan

Version 1

Raw-material industries per resource area, processing industries near medium and large towns (by the cost of
their inputs), demand per town, names after the nearest place. Outputs the industry list, the map editor's import
files (towns and industries; towns with their demand only) and a preview.

Inputs: `grid: industry_grid`, `maps: resource_maps`, `rules: industry_rules`, `places: osm_points`, `frame: map_frame`  
Outputs: `industries: industry_list`, `lua: text_document`, `towns_lua: text_document`, `preview: image`

Parameters:

- `industries` ([IndustrySettings](#industrysettings), required): The industry planning (from the climate preset).
- `ignore_town_size` (boolean, default `false`): industries.plan only: all towns equal (they start at the same size): each is medium with plan.equal_town_slots factories and gets one long-distance cargo (commercial/industrial in turns).
- `industry_density` (number, default `1.0`, > 0): Multiplies plan.production_per_type, plan.max_per_type and the number of areas per resource (rounded, at least 1 each).
- `all_cargos` (boolean, default `false`): Resources without a fitting area get areas anyway, regardless of land cover and height (unrealistic; fish excluded); processing industries whose inputs have no source on the map are placed anyway.

## industries.resource_areas

Version 1

Building sites per kind and resource areas from the terrain the game will see (`heights` = decoded heightmap,
`heightmap` = its pixels, 0 = real water core) and the layers; towns keep their distance.

Inputs: `heights: field`, `heightmap: image`, `black_m: number`, `map_format: map_format`, `forest: mask`, `meadow: mask`, `cropland: mask`, `rock: mask`, `glacier: mask`, `water: mask`, `shore: mask`, `mountains: mask`, `towns: town_list`  
Outputs: `grid: industry_grid`, `maps: resource_maps`, `resources_preview: image`, `sites_preview: image`

Parameters:

- `industries` ([IndustrySettings](#industrysettings), required): The industry planning (from the climate preset).
- `ignore_town_size` (boolean, default `false`): industries.plan only: all towns equal (they start at the same size): each is medium with plan.equal_town_slots factories and gets one long-distance cargo (commercial/industrial in turns).
- `industry_density` (number, default `1.0`, > 0): Multiplies plan.production_per_type, plan.max_per_type and the number of areas per resource (rounded, at least 1 each).
- `all_cargos` (boolean, default `false`): Resources without a fitting area get areas anyway, regardless of land cover and height (unrealistic; fish excluded); processing industries whose inputs have no source on the map are placed anyway.

- `work_scale` (integer, default `2`, >= 1): Result has 1/work_scale of the heightmap resolution.

- `scale` (number, default `1.0`, >= 1, <= 10): Scale 1:scale for distances - game metres per real metre = 1 / scale.
- `height_scale` (number \| none, default `null`): Scale 1:height_scale for heights; None = like `scale`, 1 = real heights, below 1 = higher than real. Slopes in game get scale / height_scale times steeper.

## mask.above

Version 1

Pixels whose value is above the limit.

Inputs: `field: field`  
Outputs: `mask: mask`

Parameters:

- `limit` (number, required): The pixel is set where the value is above (`mask.above`) or below (`mask.below`) this limit.

## mask.all

Version 1

Pixels set in every linked mask.

Inputs: `masks: mask` (many)  
Outputs: `mask: mask`

## mask.any

Version 1

Pixels set in at least one linked mask.

Pixels whose value is below the limit.

- `limit` (number, required): The pixel is set where the value is above (`mask.above`) or below (`mask.below`) this limit.

## mask.invert

Version 1

Pixels not set in the mask.

Inputs: `mask: mask`  
Outputs: `mask: mask`

## mask.near

Version 1

Pixels at most `distance_px` from the mask (the mask grown by a distance); empty for an empty mask.

Inputs: `mask: mask`  
Outputs: `mask: mask`

Parameters:

- `distance_px` (number, default `1.0`, >= 0): Distance in pixels of the mask (heightmap grid: 1 px = 4 game m).

## mask.smooth

Version 1

Majority filter: a pixel is set where more than `threshold` of its surroundings are set.

Inputs: `mask: mask`  
Outputs: `mask: mask`

Parameters:

- `radius_m` (number, default `80.0`, unit m, > 0): Gaussian radius (real metres): small specks vanish, borders become rounder.
- `threshold` (number, default `0.5`, > 0, < 1): Share of set pixels around a pixel from which it stays set.

## mask.subtract

Version 1

Pixels of `mask` set in none of the `minus` masks (e.g. no forest on water).

Inputs: `mask: mask`, `minus: mask` (many)  
Outputs: `mask: mask`

Version 1

The mask on the heightmap grid (nearest neighbour), e.g. for the game's import layers.

Outputs: `mask: mask`

Highways of the given types touching the map, with all tags.

Nodes with one of the tags inside the map (places by default).

Waterways touching the map, without tunnels and culverts; unnamed ways get the name of their river relation.

## paths.plan

Version 1

Field tracks (only paved; in forest and settlement only main tracks) and hiking paths (mountain trails always,
others only paved) from OSM; cut at the map edge, at `blocked` (water, glacier) and - except main ways - in
`restricted` (forest, settlement) and town areas.

Inputs: `ways: osm_lines`, `places: osm_points`, `frame: map_frame`, `blocked: mask` (many), `restricted: mask`  
Outputs: `paths: path_plan`

Parameters:

- `track_types` (list of string, default `["track"]`): OSM highway values of field and forest tracks.
- `trail_types` (list of string, default `["path", "footway", "bridleway"]`): OSM highway values of hiking paths.
- `only_paved` (boolean, default `true`): Only paved ways (track grades or paved surfaces).
- `track_grades` (list of string, default `["grade1", "grade2", "grade3"]`): tracktype values that count as paved.
- `paved_surfaces` (list of string, default `["paved", "asphalt", "concrete", "paving_stones", "sett", "compacted", "fine_gravel", "gravel"]`): surface values that count as paved.
- `skip_private` (boolean, default `true`): Leave out access=private/no.
- `trail_sac_scales` (list of string, default `["hiking", "mountain_hiking", "demanding_mountain_hiking", "alpine_hiking"]`): Mountain trails with these sac_scale values always (any surface, also in forest and settlement).
- `main_track_grades` (list of string, default `["grade1"]`): In forest and settlement only main tracks: these grades ...
- `main_named` (boolean, default `true`): ... or named tracks ...
- `main_surfaces` (list of string, default `["paved", "asphalt", "concrete", "paving_stones", "sett"]`): ... or these surfaces (trails never).
- `town_radius_m` (table of number): Built-up area = circle around OSM places per kind (real metres); {} = none.
- `densify_m` (number, default `10.0`, unit m, > 0): Sample the ways this finely before cutting (real metres).
- `simplify_m` (number, default `4.0`, unit m, >= 0): Simplification (real metres, about half the heightmap resolution).
- `min_length_m` (number, default `60.0`, unit m, >= 0): Shorter pieces are left out (real metres).

## paths.preview

Version 1

Tracks brown, trails orange on the preview base.

Inputs: `base: image`, `paths: path_plan`  
Outputs: `image: image`

Parameters:

- `track_color` ([integer, integer, integer], default `[140, 85, 30]`): Colour of field tracks.
- `trail_color` ([integer, integer, integer], default `[255, 150, 0]`): Colour of hiking paths.

## paths.terrain

Version 1

Terrain under the paths: level across (terrace on slopes, slight hollow), smooth transition to the side; water
and its border (`keep_free`) and the country roads (`road_core`) stay as they are.

Inputs: `heights: field`, `paths: path_plan`, `keep_free: mask`, `road_core: mask`, `map_format: map_format`  
Outputs: `heights: field`

Parameters:

- `width_game_m` (table of number): Width per path kind (game m).
- `sink_game_m` (number, default `0.25`, unit game m): Lower the path by this much.
- `profile_smooth_game_m` (number, default `20.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Smooth the longitudinal profile of the path.
- `max_change_game_m` (number, default `1.5`, unit game m, >= 0): Change the terrain at most this much.
- `blend_px` (number, default `1.5`, > 0): Transition to the side (heightmap pixels).

## riverbed.groove

Version 1

Groove along the centre line: depth relative to the terrain (follows its slope), soft flanks, never below the
water line + 1 m (game). It makes a painted river look like a river course.

Inputs: `heights: field`, `centre: mask`, `land_min_m: number`, `map_format: map_format`  
Outputs: `heights: field`

Parameters:

- `depth_game_m` (number, default `4.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Depth of the groove (0 = none).
- `width_game_m` (number, default `4.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Flat bottom.
- `smooth_game_m` (number, default `8.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Cosine flanks.

## riverbed.landcover

Version 1

Landcover cells more than half covered by the painted riverbed get the riverbed class (water and shore stay).

Inputs: `landcover: classes`, `bed: mask`  
Outputs: `landcover: classes`

Parameters:

- `riverbed_class` (integer, default `210`, >= 0, <= 255): Own landcover class of the painted riverbed.
- `shore_class` (integer, default `200`, >= 0, <= 255): Own landcover class of the shore (stays).

## riverbed.paint

Version 1

The painted riverbed pieces as a mask, not on water and its border (`no_cover`); `centre` = 1-pixel centre
line for the groove.

Inputs: `beds: bed_segments`, `no_cover: mask`  
Outputs: `bed: mask`, `centre: mask`

## riverbed.ramp

Version 1

Ramp where a painted riverbed meets real water: along the bed (`bed`) the terrain falls linearly over
`length_game_m` to the water line + 1 m (game) at the real water (`real`), the terrain beside it follows within
the corridor. Only lowers; beds that never meet real water stay as they are.

Inputs: `heights: field`, `bed: mask`, `real: mask`, `land_min_m: number`, `map_format: map_format`  
Outputs: `heights: field`

Parameters:

- `length_game_m` (number, default `0.0`, unit game m, >= 0): The riverbed falls linearly to the water line over this length before it meets real water (0 = no ramp).
- `corridor_game_m` (number, default `60.0`, unit game m, >= 0): The terrain beside the ramp follows it this far on each side (cosine falloff).

## rivers.plan

Version 1

Continuous rivers from OSM: real and painted water, widths, weirs (no terrain change). `heights` = original
elevation on the heightmap grid, `floor` = valley floor (lowest height around), `water` = WorldCover water (the
width of real rivers follows it).

Inputs: `ways: osm_ways`, `frame: map_frame`, `heights: field`, `floor: field`, `water: mask`, `land_min_m: number`  
Outputs: `plan: river_plan`, `preview: image`, `profiles: image`

Parameters:

- `real_water_until_m` (number \| none, default `null`, unit m): Real water (game water) only up to this height above sea level (the region's "real water up to"); None = 120 m above the lowest land. Higher = more real water, but real water is cut down to the water line (deep trenches).
- `real_water_rivers` ("all" \| "navigable", default `"all"`): Which waterways may be real water: "all" (below the limit) or only "navigable" ones (CEMT class, a name in `navigable_names`, unnamed canals attached to them); other rivers stay painted water, also in flat land.
- `navigable_names` (list of string, default `[]`): Waterways whose name starts with one of these count as navigable (case-insensitive), e.g. ("Dortmund-Ems-Kanal", "Mittellandkanal") where OSM has no CEMT class.
- `min_real_run_game_m` (number, default `1000.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Shorter connected pieces where real water is possible do not count (tolerance).
- `min_width_game_m` (number, default `60.0`, unit game m, > 0): Real water: width at least.
- `max_width_game_m` (number, default `300.0`, unit game m, > 0): Real water: width at most (in lakes the water layer shapes, not the river).
- `painted_width_game_m` ([number, number], default `[10.0, 20.0]`): Painted riverbed: the width varies between these values (game m).
- `painted_width_wave_game_m` (number, default `400.0`, unit game m, > 0): Painted riverbed: the width varies over about this distance.
- `painted_width_seed` (integer, default `7`): Random seed of the painted width.
- `floor_smooth_passes` (integer, default `20`, >= 0): Smoothing of the valley floor along the course (mean with the neighbours).
- `weir_min_drop_m` (number, default `2.0`, unit m, >= 0): Smaller steps at the transition painted -> real are not reported as weirs.
- `preview_width` (integer, default `2000`, >= 100): Width of the preview picture in pixels.
- `profile_rivers` (integer, default `4`, >= 0): Height profiles of the rivers with the longest continuous main course.

## rivers.to_valley

Version 1

The river plan with the painted rivers moved into the valley line of `heights` (original elevation on the
heightmap grid); the preview shows the moved courses coloured by the size of the move.

Inputs: `plan: river_plan`, `heights: field`  
Outputs: `plan: river_plan`, `preview: image`

Parameters:

- `max_move_real_m` (number, default `100.0`, unit m, >= 0): The painted riverbed may move at most this far beside the OSM course (real metres; 0 = keep OSM).
- `lower_per_100m_m` (number, default `3.0`, unit m, >= 0): A move pays only where the bed gets lower by more than this per 100 m of move (keeps OSM where the valley is flat).
- `max_bend` (number, default `0.5`, > 0, <= 1): Sideways change of the move per metre along the course at most (smooth course).
- `smooth_real_m` (number, default `60.0`, unit m, >= 0): The move is averaged over this distance along the course.
- `preview_width` (integer, default `2000`, >= 100): Width of the preview picture in pixels.

## roads.from_osm

Version 1

Country roads for the terrain: OSM roads of the classes, joined where OSM splits them, cut at the map edge,
bridges/tunnels, town areas, closed settlement (`settlement` = WorldCover settlement) and water.

Inputs: `ways: osm_lines`, `places: osm_points`, `frame: map_frame`, `water: mask`, `settlement: mask`  
Outputs: `roads: road_lines`

Parameters:

- `road_types` (list of string, default `["trunk", "primary", "secondary", "tertiary", "unclassified"]`): OSM highway classes (widths: the road terrain node).
- `include_links` (boolean, default `true`): Links (<class>_link) count as the class.
- `skip_bridges` (boolean, default `true`): Leave out bridge=* (except no) - else a dam across the valley.
- `skip_tunnels` (boolean, default `true`): Leave out tunnel=* / covered=yes - else a trench over the mountain.
- `town_radius_m` (table of number): Left out inside towns: circle per place kind (real metres, 0 = none).
- `settlement_radius_m` (number, default `100.0`, unit m, > 0): Closed settlement only: share of WorldCover settlement within this radius (real metres) ...
- `settlement_share` (number, default `0.5`, >= 0, <= 1): ... at least this (roads themselves are often settlement in WorldCover).
- `densify_m` (number, default `10.0`, unit m, > 0): Sample the roads this finely before cutting (real metres).
- `simplify_m` (number, default `4.0`, unit m, >= 0): Simplification (real metres).
- `min_length_m` (number, default `80.0`, unit m, >= 0): Shorter pieces are dropped after merging (real metres).

## roads.network

Version 1

Roads between the towns and to the industries through the terrain (`heights`, real m on the heightmap grid;
`water` = painted and real water with shore, `riverbed`), with bridges and tunnels; water and riverbeds with a
margin are crossed by bridges only. Node heights in game metres above `land_min_m`. The terrain under the normal
ways is shaped (`heights`, `core` = pixels at full weight); the preview draws the network on `base`.

Inputs: `heights: field`, `water: mask`, `riverbed: mask`, `forest: mask`, `rock: mask`, `glacier: mask`, `towns: town_list`, `industries: industry_list`, `map_format: map_format`, `land_min_m: number`, `base: image`  
Outputs: `plan: road_plan`, `heights: field`, `core: mask`, `preview: image`

Parameters:

- `min_capacity` (integer, default `0`, >= 0): Towns with a smaller start size get no road.
- `max_link_game_m` (number, default `16000.0`, unit game m, > 0): Longer links between towns are not planned.
- `detour_via_factor` (number, default `1.2`, >= 1): Link A-B is dropped if A-C-B is at most this much longer.
- `max_route_detour` (number, default `2.5`, >= 1): Route at most this much longer than the straight line, else no road.
- `connect_industries` (boolean, default `true`): Every industry gets a spur to the nearest road or town.
- `max_spur_game_m` (number, default `2500.0`, unit game m, > 0): Industries farther from a road or town get no spur.
- `town_radius_game_m` (number, default `150.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Roads end this far from the town centre (the town's own streets take over).
- `industry_clearance_game_m` (number, default `80.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Spurs end this far from the industry.
- `cell_game_m` (number, default `25.0`, unit game m, > 0): Grid cell of the fine route search.
- `coarse_cell_game_m` (number, default `100.0`, unit game m, > 0): Grid cell of the coarse route search over the whole map.
- `serpentine_factor` (number, default `2.0`, >= 1): Coarse search: mean grades up to this many times max_grade (the fine route winds up in serpentines).
- `corridor_game_m` (number, default `150.0`, unit game m, > 0): The fine route stays this close to the coarse route ...
- `corridor_widenings` (integer, default `2`, >= 0): ... and the corridor is doubled this often if no route fits.
- `min_radius_game_m` (number, default `25.0`, unit game m, > 0): Smallest curve radius.
- `max_grade` (number, default `0.2`, > 0): Steepest grade (height / distance).
- `slope_weight` (number, default `2.0`): Surcharge for the grade (at max_grade: cost x 1 + slope_weight).
- `climb_weight` (number, default `3.0`, >= 0): Cost per metre of height gained or lost (in metres of road): steady grades and a curve more instead of up and down.
- `turn_weight` (number, default `0.3`): Surcharge per radian of turning (in cells of length); keeps the line calm.
- `forest_cost` (number, default `0.3`): Surcharge per forest share.
- `rock_cost` (number, default `1.0`): Surcharge per rock share.
- `glacier_limit` (number, default `0.5`): Cells with more glacier are blocked.
- `wet_margin_game_m` (number, default `50.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Water (painted and real), shore and riverbeds plus this margin form the wet zone: crossed by bridges only.
- `wet_clearance_game_m` (number, default `10.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Bridges lie at least this high above water and riverbeds (real water: above its surface).
- `valley_game_m` (number, default `150.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Near the wet zone the ground costs more (rather higher up the slope than down by the river) ...
- `valley_cost` (number, default `1.0`): ... up to this surcharge at the zone, falling to 0 at valley_game_m.
- `reuse_factor` (number, default `0.3`, > 0, <= 1): Planned roads cost only this much (bundling).
- `max_structure_game_m` (number, default `400.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Longest straight structure move of the route search (bridge, tunnel, fill or cut).
- `bridge_cost` (number, default `10.0`): Surcharge per metre of bridge ...
- `bridge_height_cost` (number, default `0.5`, >= 0): ... plus this per metre of bridge and metre of height above the ground (high bridges cost more).
- `fill_cost` (number, default `0.2`, >= 0): Surcharge per metre of fill and metre of height (below bridge_from_game_m; cheaper than a bridge).
- `cut_cost` (number, default `0.25`, >= 0): Surcharge per metre of cut and metre of depth (above tunnel_from_game_m; cheaper than a tunnel).
- `tunnel_cost` (number, default `12.0`): Surcharge per metre of tunnel.
- `structure_fixed_game_m` (number, default `300.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Fixed cost of a bridge or tunnel (abutments, portals) as metres of road.
- `structure_max_grade` (number, default `0.06`, > 0): Bridges and tunnels at most this steep (they cross; the road climbs on the ground).
- `straighten_game_m` (number, default `10.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Straighten the zigzag of the grid up to this deviation.
- `sample_game_m` (number, default `4.0`, unit game m, > 0): Sample the line this finely (profile, terrain).
- `node_game_m` (number, default `12.0`, unit game m, > 0): Distance of the plan's nodes.
- `profile_smooth_game_m` (number, default `120.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Smooth the longitudinal profile of the normal road (long = steady grades; fills and cuts take the rest).
- `approach_smooth_game_m` (number, default `30.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Smooth the approaches to bridges and tunnels.
- `bridge_from_game_m` (number, default `10.0`, unit game m, > 0): Bridge where the road lies this much above the ground; below a fill.
- `tunnel_from_game_m` (number, default `12.0`, unit game m, > 0): Tunnel where the road lies this much below the ground; above a cut.
- `min_bridge_game_m` (number, default `30.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Shorter bridges become fills (not over water).
- `min_tunnel_game_m` (number, default `150.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Shorter tunnels become cuts.
- `max_span_extend_game_m` (number, default `60.0`, unit game m, >= 0): A bridge or tunnel span grows at most this far beyond its leg of the route search (to the rim of a gorge: the legs end on the cells of the search grid).
- `max_structure_gap_game_m` (number, default `40.0`, unit game m, >= 0): Normal pieces between two bridges (tunnels) up to this length become part of them.
- `end_blend_game_m` (number, default `60.0`, unit game m, >= 0): At junctions and ends the profile meets the ground height over this length.
- `width_game_m` (number, default `14.0`, unit game m, > 0): Width of the levelled strip under the road (carriageway and walkways).
- `bank_slope` (number, default `0.6`, > 0): Bank slope (height / width) of the terrain beside the road.
- `blend_min_px` (number, default `1.5`, > 0): Transition to the side at least (heightmap pixels).
- `preview_width` (integer, default `2000`, >= 100): Width of the preview picture in pixels.
